text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Fisheries Minister Karl Eirik Schjoett-Pedersen says Norway has rejected all claims from the EU on subsidizing and dumping of salmon. Schjoett-Pedersen says Norwegian authorities have cooperated with EU's investigation into the claims.
- DNO ASA, a small oil company, is the winner of the year on the Oslo Bourse. In 1996 the price per share in DNO has shot up almost 500 percent.

- While most Norwegians are concerned about the increasing prices on electricity, 20 landowners in Oldereid in Northern Norway have free electricity. When Oldereid got electricity in 1918, landowners sold property to Oldereid power suppliers in return for free electricity for ever.

- Travel agencies are concerned about a dramatic fall in profitability because Scandinavian Airline System (SAS) has cut the commission from eigth to five percent on domestic flights and from nine to five percent on inter-Scandinavian fligths.
- More and more Norwegians buy shares in mutual funds in order to profit from regulations giving them a tax break.
